about.pageTitle: About Chill — Secure Remote Access App Ecosystem
about.description: Learn about Chill, an ecosystem of apps for securely accessing your machines from anywhere. Our mission, our approach, and our commitments.
about.title: About Chill
about.mission.title: Our Mission
about.mission.content: Chill has a simple goal: let anyone access their machines from anywhere, securely. Whether it's waking up a PC remotely, launching an SSH terminal from your phone, or managing your connections — our apps are designed so your data stays on your devices, not on third-party servers.
about.story.title: Why Chill Exists
about.story.content: Chill is an ecosystem of apps built around one idea: managing data differently. Today, most services centralize everything on servers that don't always guarantee full security. Chill takes a different approach, built on SSH and Tailscale — direct, encrypted connections between your devices, with no middleman. ChillShell is the mobile SSH terminal, Chill is the desktop app that sets everything up in a few clicks.
about.values.title: What We Stand For
about.values.securityDesc: SSH keys are stored using your device's hardware-backed encryption. PINs are hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 following NIST SP 800-132 guidelines. Key-based authentication is the OWASP-recommended standard for SSH access.
about.values.privacyDesc: Our apps collect zero user data. No analytics, no tracking, no telemetry. Your credentials never leave your device. This isn't an option — it's the foundation of our architecture.
about.values.transparencyDesc: We conduct rigorous internal security reviews and document our practices. No external audit has been performed to date — and we say so clearly. Transparency also means being honest about what hasn't been done yet.
about.dev.title: Built by a Maker, for Everyone
about.dev.content: Chill is developed by an independent creator based in France. Not a professional developer, but someone who builds useful tools from real needs. Every feature is designed to solve a real problem — not to check a marketing box.

tutos.tailscale.title: Tailscale VPN
tutos.tailscale.intro: Tailscale lets you connect to your PC from anywhere — WiFi, 5G, abroad. No port forwarding needed.
tutos.tailscale.step1.title: Create a Tailscale account
tutos.tailscale.step1.content: Go to the Tailscale website and create a free account. You can sign in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub, or Apple.
tutos.tailscale.step2.title: Install Tailscale on your PC
tutos.tailscale.win.step2.content: Download Tailscale from the official website and install it. Sign in with the same account you just created.
tutos.tailscale.win.step2.connectedNote: Once installed, Tailscale appears in your system tray. You'll see "Connected" and your device's Tailscale IP.
tutos.tailscale.linux.step2.code:
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up
tutos.tailscale.mac.step2.content: Download from the Mac App Store or tailscale.com. Sign in with the same account.
tutos.tailscale.step3.title: Install on your phone
tutos.tailscale.step3.content: Download Tailscale on your phone and sign in with the same account as on your PC.
tutos.tailscale.step4.title: Get your Tailscale IP
tutos.tailscale.step4.content: Your Tailscale IP starts with 100.x.x.x — you can find it in the app or the web dashboard. Use this IP in ChillShell instead of your local IP. It works everywhere: WiFi, 5G, abroad.
tutos.bios.title: BIOS Setup (Wake-on-LAN)
tutos.bios.intro: To use Wake-on-LAN, your BIOS needs specific settings enabled. The exact names vary by brand, but here's what to look for.
tutos.bios.generic.title: What to look for
tutos.bios.generic.content: Look for these settings (names vary by brand): "Wake on LAN", "Power On By PCI-E", "ErP Ready" (must be Disabled), "Resume by LAN", "Wake Up on LAN", "Native ASPM" (must be Disabled).
tutos.bios.asus.title: ASUS / ROG
tutos.bios.asus.warning: These screenshots are from an ASUS ROG motherboard. Menu names and paths vary depending on your motherboard brand and model.
tutos.bios.asus.step1: Enter BIOS by pressing DEL or F2 at boot, then switch to Advanced Mode (F7).
tutos.bios.asus.step3: Set ErP Ready to Disabled and Power On By PCI-E to Enabled.
tutos.bios.asus.step4: Go back, then go to Advanced > Platform Misc Configuration.
tutos.wol.title: Wake-on-LAN
tutos.wol.intro: Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely from ChillShell.
tutos.wol.warning: Important: Wake-on-LAN only works on the local network via Ethernet cable. WiFi is not supported.
tutos.wol.step1.title: Enable in BIOS
tutos.wol.step1.content: See the BIOS Setup tutorial to enable the required settings.
tutos.wol.win.step2.title: Enable in Windows
tutos.wol.win.step2.intro: Open Device Manager and find your Ethernet adapter under Network adapters.
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub1.title: Advanced tab: Wake on Magic Packet
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub1.content: Right-click your Ethernet adapter > Properties > Advanced tab. Find "Wake on Magic Packet" and set it to Enabled.
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub2.title: Power Management tab
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub2.content: Go to the Power Management tab. Check "Allow this device to wake the computer" and "Only allow a magic packet to wake the computer".
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub3.title: Disable Fast Startup
tutos.wol.win.step2.sub3.content: Fast Startup can prevent Wake-on-LAN from working. To disable it: Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do > Change settings that are currently unavailable > Uncheck "Turn on fast startup".
tutos.wol.win.step2.powershellCode:
# Check which devices can wake the PC
powercfg /devicequery wake_armed

# Disable Fast Startup via registry
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power" /v HiberbootEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
tutos.wol.win.step3.graphicalContent: Open Settings > Network & Internet > Ethernet. Scroll down to find your physical (MAC) address.

security.title: Security
security.simple.keys: Your SSH keys stay on your phone. Never sent anywhere.
security.simple.pin: PIN hashed, never stored in plaintext
security.simple.noData: No data transmitted to our servers
security.detail.storage.title: Data storage
security.detail.storage.content: SSH keys and credentials are stored using flutter_secure_storage: AES-CBC on Android (EncryptedSharedPreferences), Keychain on iOS. The master encryption key is stored in the hardware-backed keystore, which means it cannot be extracted even with root access. According to OWASP Mobile Security guidelines, hardware-backed key storage is the recommended approach for securing cryptographic material on mobile devices.
security.detail.ssh.title: SSH connection
security.detail.ssh.content: ChillShell uses the SSH protocol with Trust On First Use (TOFU) for host verification, as defined in RFC 4251. Ed25519 is the preferred key algorithm, recommended by the OpenSSH project for its strong security with compact key sizes (256-bit). Keys are loaded into memory only during the active session, then securely disposed via SecureBuffer to minimize exposure in RAM.
security.detail.auth.title: Local authentication
security.detail.auth.content: Your PIN is hashed with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 using 100,000 iterations, following NIST Special Publication 800-132 recommendations for password-based key derivation. Biometric unlock is available via the device's local_auth framework. The app auto-locks after a configurable period of inactivity, ensuring protection even if you set your phone down.
security.detail.leaks.title: Leak protection
security.detail.leaks.content: Command history is filtered using regex patterns to prevent accidental storage of passwords or tokens. The clipboard auto-cleans after sensitive copy operations. On Android, FLAG_SECURE is enabled to prevent screenshots and screen recording of the terminal session. These measures align with OWASP MASVS (Mobile Application Security Verification Standard) data protection requirements.
security.detail.root.title: Root/jailbreak detection
security.detail.root.content: At launch, ChillShell checks common root paths and jailbreak indicators. If a compromised environment is detected, a warning banner is displayed. The app remains functional to respect user choice, but the warning ensures informed consent about potential security risks on rooted or jailbroken devices.
security.detail.audit.title: Audit log
security.detail.audit.content: All security-relevant events are logged locally with timestamps, including login attempts, session starts and ends, and key generation events. The log uses FIFO rotation at 500 entries to balance auditability with storage efficiency. Logs never leave the device and can be reviewed in the app settings.
security.detail.limits.title: Known limitations
security.detail.limits.content: SecureBuffer cannot guarantee that the garbage collector won't create copies of sensitive data in memory. Root detection can be bypassed on devices with advanced rooting tools like Magisk Hide. These limitations are documented here for full transparency — we believe honest disclosure of trade-offs builds more trust than hiding them.
security.detail.scores.title: Audit results
security.detail.scores.content: ChillShell has undergone a thorough internal white-box security audit covering source code, data storage, network communications, and authentication flows. The STRIDE threat model analysis achieved 100% mitigation across all six threat categories (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, Elevation of Privilege). Full audit methodology and reports are available on request for security researchers and enterprise evaluators.
security.source.owasp: According to OWASP Mobile Security Project guidelines, hardware-backed keystores and key-based SSH authentication are the recommended standards for securing mobile terminal applications.
security.source.nist: Following NIST Special Publication 800-132 recommendations, ChillShell implements PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with 100,000 iterations for PIN hashing — exceeding the minimum threshold recommended for 2026.
security.source.rfc: ChillShell implements SSH as defined in RFC 4253 (Transport Layer Protocol) and RFC 4252 (Authentication Protocol), using Ed25519 keys as recommended by the OpenSSH project.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Which devices do Chill and ChillShell run on?
faq.a1: ChillShell is available on Android. No testing has been done on iOS yet — support is planned but not yet validated. Chill runs on Windows and Linux. macOS has not been tested yet. We'll update this page as soon as testing is complete.
faq.q2: What's the difference between Chill and ChillShell?
faq.a2: ChillShell is the mobile app (Android) — a full SSH terminal to connect to your computer from your phone. Chill is the desktop companion app (Windows, Linux) that automates the setup: SSH server, Wake-on-LAN, and Tailscale VPN. Both apps are free.
faq.a3: Yes, both Chill and ChillShell are completely free. No subscription, no hidden fees, no in-app purchases. All features are included at no cost.
faq.q4: What is Tailscale and why use it?
faq.a4: Tailscale is a free VPN that creates a private encrypted network between your devices. It lets you access your computer from anywhere — coffee shop, office, another city — not just your local WiFi. ChillShell has Tailscale built in. Chill configures it automatically on your desktop.
faq.q5: Can I access my computer outside my local network?
faq.a5: Yes, with Tailscale. Without it, SSH only works when your phone and computer are on the same WiFi. Tailscale creates a secure tunnel that works from anywhere with an internet connection. Setup takes under 2 minutes with our apps.
faq.a6: No. Both Chill and ChillShell operate on a zero data collection policy. All data — SSH keys, credentials, session history — stays exclusively on your devices. No analytics, no telemetry, no tracking. SSH connections are direct between your phone and your computer with no intermediary.
faq.q7: Which server OS does ChillShell work with?
faq.a7: ChillShell works with any operating system that has an SSH server enabled: Windows 10/11 with OpenSSH, all modern Linux distributions (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch), and macOS with Remote Login. Our OS Setup tutorial walks you through enabling SSH in under 5 minutes.
faq.q8: Does it work with Claude Code / Codex CLI / Cursor?
faq.a8: Yes, ChillShell fully supports all major CLI agents via SSH: Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex CLI (OpenAI), Cursor CLI, and Kimi Code (Moonshot AI). You can run any terminal-based AI agent directly from your phone. Check our CLI Agents page for the full compatibility table.
faq.a9: No, Wake-on-LAN requires a wired Ethernet connection on the target PC. This is a hardware limitation — the network adapter must be powered to receive the magic packet. Your phone sends the packet via WiFi, but the PC must be connected by Ethernet cable.
faq.q10: Can I use ChillShell without Wake-on-LAN?
faq.a10: Absolutely. Wake-on-LAN is optional. ChillShell works perfectly as a standalone SSH terminal. You can connect to any machine with SSH enabled — on your local network or remotely via Tailscale. Many users rely solely on SSH and Tailscale without ever configuring Wake-on-LAN.
faq.a11: Chill is the desktop companion app for ChillShell. It runs on Windows and Linux. It automates everything you'd normally do manually: enabling the SSH server, configuring the firewall, setting up Wake-on-LAN, and installing Tailscale. One click instead of terminal commands.
faq.q12: Which operating systems does Chill support?
faq.a12: Chill runs on Windows 10/11 and Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch and derivatives). macOS has not been tested yet. It automatically detects your system and adapts the configuration — the right package manager, the right service manager, the right firewall rules.
faq.q13: Why does Chill need administrator rights?
faq.a13: Configuring SSH, Wake-on-LAN, and firewall rules requires system-level access on every operating system. Chill asks for your admin password once per operation, groups all commands into a single secure script, and never stores your password. See our Security page for details.
faq.a14: Yes. Chill configures your computer independently. Once SSH is enabled by Chill, you can connect from any SSH client — not just ChillShell. However, the two apps are designed to work together: Chill sets up the server side, ChillShell connects from your phone.
